items.q: A backsight of 1.9 m is taken on a point of reduced level 80 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 80 + 1.9 = 81.9 m.

items.q: The fore bearing of a line is 285 degrees. Calculate its back bearing.
items.s: Subtract 180 degrees: 285 - 180 = 105 degrees.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 5 cm represents 5000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 5 cm to 500000 cm, that is 1 in 100000 = 0.001.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 30 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 35 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 30 x 0.0000112 x 15 = 0.005 m.

items.q: A tape of length 50 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 400000 N. It is used with a pull 40 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 40 x 50 / 400000 = 0.005 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.3 N per metre is suspended between supports 50 m apart with a pull of 120 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.3 squared x 50 cubed / (24 x 120 squared) = 0.0326 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 100 m reads 2 m and the foresight on the next point reads 2.8 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 100 + 2 = 102 m; reduced level = 102 - 2.8 = 99.2 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.85, 1.05 m and the falls recorded are 0.5, 0.65 m. The first point has a reduced level of 50 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 1.9 - 1.15 = 0.75 m, so the last reduced level is 50 + 0.75 = 50.75 m.

items.q: In levelling, the combined correction for curvature and refraction at a distance of 0.5 km is found from 0.0673 D squared. Calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = 0.0673 x 0.5 squared = 0.0168 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 1.2 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 1.26 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (1.2 + 1.26)/2 = 1.23 m.

items.q: Convert the whole circle bearing of 40 degrees to a quadrantal bearing.
items.s: The bearing lies in the northeast quadrant, so the quadrantal bearing is 40 degrees NE.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 160 degrees and 335 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 175 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 175 degrees.

items.q: The magnetic bearing of a line is 70 degrees and the magnetic declination at the place is 6 degrees east. Calculate the true bearing.
items.s: For easterly declination the true bearing is greater than the magnetic bearing: 70 + 6 = 76 degrees.

items.q: A traverse line is 120 m long and its bearing is 45 degrees. Calculate its departure in metres.
items.s: Departure = length x sine of the bearing = 120 x sin 45 = 84.85 m.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 1000 m and N 1200 m. A line of length 90 m is run on a bearing of 20 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 90 x sin 20 = 30.78 m, so the new easting = 1000 + 30.78 = 1031 m.

items.q: A closed traverse gives a total error in latitude of 300 m and a total error in departure of 300 m. Calculate the linear misclosure in metres.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (300 squared + 300 squared) = 424.3 m.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 1200 m has a closing error of 0.5 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 1200 / 0.5 = 1 in 2400.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 5 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 60 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (5 - 2) x 180 = 540 degrees, so the measured angles are 541 degrees and the misclosure is 60 minutes.

items.q: A traverse of total length 800 m has a total error in departure of 0.8 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 100 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.8 x (100/800) = 0.1 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 120 m and a perpendicular height of 45 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 120 x 45 = 2700 square metres.

items.q: The offsets taken at 15 m intervals from a base line are 5, 4, 2, 3, 7 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 15[(5 + 7)/2 + 9] = 225 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 10 m intervals are 2, 2, 5, 6, 6 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 166.7 square metres.

items.q: The cross sectional areas at the two ends of a cutting 30 m long are 40 and 30 square metres. Using the end area method, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = length x (first area + last area)/2 = 30 x (40 + 30)/2 = 1050 cubic metres.

items.q: In a cutting 40 m long the end areas are 20 and 40 square metres and the mid section area is 38 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 40/6[(20 + 40) + 4 x 38] = 1413 cubic metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 25 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 10 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (10/25) x 100 = 40 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through an angle of 30 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 200 x tan 15 = 53.59 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m turns through a deflection angle of 90 degrees. Calculate the length of the curve in metres.
items.s: Length = pi x R x deflection / 180 = 3.1416 x 150 x 90 / 180 = 235.6 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 250 m deflects through 40 degrees. Calculate the length of the long chord in metres.
items.s: Long chord = 2R sin(deflection/2) = 2 x 250 x sin 20 = 171 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m deflects through 90 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 100[1 - cos 45] = 29.29 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through 60 degrees. Calculate the external distance in metres.
items.s: External = R[sec(deflection/2) - 1] = 200[sec 30 - 1] = 30.94 m.

items.q: A circular curve has a radius of 250 m. Taking the degree of curve as the angle subtended at the centre by an arc of 30 m, calculate that angle in degrees.
items.s: Degree of curve = 1718.87 / R = 1718.87 / 250 = 6.88 degrees.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 100 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 40 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 40 squared / (2 x 100) = 8 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 1000. A line on the plan measures 12 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 12 cm x 1000 = 12000 cm = 12000 m.

items.q: A backsight of 1.35 m is taken on a point of reduced level 125 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 125 + 1.35 = 126.3 m.

items.q: The fore bearing of a line is 35 degrees. Calculate its back bearing.
items.s: Add 180 degrees: 35 + 180 = 215 degrees.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 2 cm represents 10000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 2 cm to 1000000 cm, that is 1 in 500000 = 0.0002.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 50 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 28 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 50 x 0.0000112 x 8 = 0.0045 m.

items.q: A tape of length 30 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 500000 N. It is used with a pull 40 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 40 x 30 / 500000 = 0.0024 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.3 N per metre is suspended between supports 50 m apart with a pull of 100 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.3 squared x 50 cubed / (24 x 100 squared) = 0.0469 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 120 m reads 2 m and the foresight on the next point reads 1.05 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 120 + 2 = 122 m; reduced level = 122 - 1.05 = 121 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.85, 1.4 m and the falls recorded are 0.25, 0.65 m. The first point has a reduced level of 120 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 2.25 - 0.9 = 1.35 m, so the last reduced level is 120 + 1.35 = 121.3 m.

items.q: In levelling, the combined correction for curvature and refraction at a distance of 1.5 km is found from 0.0673 D squared. Calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = 0.0673 x 1.5 squared = 0.1514 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 0.4 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 0.42 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (0.4 + 0.42)/2 = 0.41 m.

items.q: Convert the whole circle bearing of 320 degrees to a quadrantal bearing.
items.s: The bearing lies in the southeast quadrant, so the quadrantal bearing is 40 degrees SE.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 110 degrees and 240 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 130 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 130 degrees.

items.q: The magnetic bearing of a line is 85 degrees and the magnetic declination at the place is 5 degrees east. Calculate the true bearing.
items.s: For easterly declination the true bearing is greater than the magnetic bearing: 85 + 5 = 90 degrees.

items.q: A traverse line is 50 m long and its bearing is 45 degrees. Calculate its latitude in metres.
items.s: Latitude = length x cosine of the bearing = 50 x cos 45 = 35.36 m.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 250 m and N 320 m. A line of length 60 m is run on a bearing of 50 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 60 x sin 50 = 45.96 m, so the new easting = 250 + 45.96 = 296 m.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 1000 m has a closing error of 0.4 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 1000 / 0.4 = 1 in 2500.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 4 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 30 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (4 - 2) x 180 = 360 degrees, so the measured angles are 360.5 degrees and the misclosure is 30 minutes.

items.q: A traverse of total length 400 m has a total error in departure of 0.4 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 50 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.4 x (50/400) = 0.05 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 50 m and a perpendicular height of 20 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 50 x 20 = 500 square metres.

items.q: The offsets taken at 10 m intervals from a base line are 6, 7, 7, 7, 6 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 10[(6 + 6)/2 + 21] = 270 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 20 m intervals are 6, 5, 5, 8, 2 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 466.7 square metres.

items.q: The cross sectional areas at the two ends of a cutting 25 m long are 30 and 50 square metres. Using the end area method, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = length x (first area + last area)/2 = 25 x (30 + 50)/2 = 1000 cubic metres.

items.q: In a cutting 30 m long the end areas are 20 and 50 square metres and the mid section area is 48 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 30/6[(20 + 50) + 4 x 48] = 1310 cubic metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 50 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 5 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (5/50) x 100 = 10 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through an angle of 40 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 200 x tan 20 = 72.79 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 60 degrees. Calculate the length of the long chord in metres.
items.s: Long chord = 2R sin(deflection/2) = 2 x 150 x sin 30 = 150 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 60 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 150[1 - cos 30] = 20.1 m.

items.q: bench mark may be defined as
o: the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the length of each line
how closely repeated measurements agree with one another
a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
items.s: bench mark: a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling. The other options describe true north, Bowditch rule, precision.

items.q: Which of the following best describes base line?
o: the longest and most carefully measured line of a chain survey from which the rest of the work is built
a bookkeeping method in which consecutive staff readings are compared to show whether the ground rose or fell
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
items.s: base line: the longest and most carefully measured line of a chain survey from which the rest of the work is built. The other options describe consecutive coordinates, true north, rise and fall.

items.q: Which term is described by “a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines”?
o: planimeter
contour interval
horizontal equivalent
trapezoidal rule
items.s: trapezoidal rule is a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines reciprocal levelling.
o: the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
items.s: reciprocal levelling: the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging. The other options describe curvature correction, line of collimation, true north.

items.q: height of instrument may be defined as
o: a short wooden stake driven into the ground to mark a station permanently
the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
a volume rule that also takes account of the mid section, giving a closer result than averaging the two ends
the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure
items.s: height of instrument: the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level. The other options describe prismoidal formula, peg, linear misclosure.

items.q: Which of the following best describes height of instrument?
o: the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports
the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
items.s: height of instrument: the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level. The other options describe latitude of a line, sag correction, true north.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines reciprocal levelling?
o: the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging
the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
items.s: reciprocal levelling: the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging. The other options describe fore bearing, deflection angle, horizontal equivalent.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines point of intersection.
o: an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure
a line measured only to prove that the plotted work is free of error
items.s: point of intersection: the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted. The other options describe planimeter, linear misclosure, check line.

items.q: Which term is described by “the distance from the point of intersection to the start or end of the curve”?
o: point of intersection
simple circular curve
versine
tangent length
items.s: tangent length is the distance from the point of intersection to the start or end of the curve.

items.q: linear error of closure may be defined as
o: software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees
the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance
a line measured only to prove that the plotted work is free of error
items.s: linear error of closure: the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance. The other options describe check line, oblique offset, geographic information system.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines prismoidal formula?
o: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
a volume rule that also takes account of the mid section, giving a closer result than averaging the two ends
the ratio of the total length traversed to the closing error, stated as one in so many
items.s: prismoidal formula: a volume rule that also takes account of the mid section, giving a closer result than averaging the two ends. The other options describe precision of a traverse, consecutive coordinates, quadrantal bearing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes temperature correction?
o: the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed
an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
a bookkeeping method in which consecutive staff readings are compared to show whether the ground rose or fell
items.s: temperature correction: the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised. The other options describe traverse, rise and fall, random error.

items.q: The statement “a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length” describes which of the following?
o: planimeter
contour
end area method
capacity of a reservoir
items.s: end area method is a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length.

items.q: sensitivity of a level may be defined as
o: a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed
the process of comparing a tape against a known standard length and recording its error
the smallest tilt of the telescope that visibly moves the bubble
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the length of each line
items.s: sensitivity of a level: the smallest tilt of the telescope that visibly moves the bubble. The other options describe traverse, Bowditch rule, standardisation of a tape.

items.q: deflection angle may be defined as
o: the constant height difference between one contour and the next
a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
a run of connected lines that returns to its starting point or closes on a known station
items.s: deflection angle: the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line. The other options describe contour interval, closed traverse, ill conditioned triangle.

items.q: The statement “an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees” describes which of the following?
o: standardisation of a tape
chain surveying
oblique offset
check line
items.s: oblique offset is an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees.

items.q: The statement “the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted” describes which of the following?
o: tangent length
point of intersection
length of curve
external distance
items.s: point of intersection is the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines total station?
o: the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle
an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
items.s: total station: an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically. The other options describe theodolite, back bearing, exterior angle.

items.q: The statement “a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees” describes which of the following?
o: exterior angle
local attraction
quadrantal bearing
magnetic declination
items.s: quadrantal bearing is a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees.

items.q: slope correction may be defined as
o: a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines
the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
the reduction applied when a distance is measured along sloping ground instead of horizontally
a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current
items.s: slope correction: the reduction applied when a distance is measured along sloping ground instead of horizontally. The other options describe trapezoidal rule, local attraction, temperature correction.

items.q: random error may be defined as
o: an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
a staff position that is read both before and after the instrument is moved
the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
items.s: random error: an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean. The other options describe total station, change point, point of intersection.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Simpson rule?
o: a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
a triangle whose angles all lie between thirty and one hundred and twenty degrees, giving the strongest fix
the angle at a station between the two lines meeting there
an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
items.s: Simpson rule: a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets. The other options describe included angle, well conditioned triangle, random error.

items.q: Which of the following best describes electronic distance measurement?
o: the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
positions of all stations measured from one common origin
an offset that meets the survey line at exactly ninety degrees
items.s: electronic distance measurement: the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal. The other options describe height of collimation, perpendicular offset, independent coordinates.

items.q: Which of the following best describes independent coordinates?
o: the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
a staff reading taken on a point that is neither a change point nor the closing sight
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
positions of all stations measured from one common origin
items.s: independent coordinates: positions of all stations measured from one common origin. The other options describe interior angle, capacity of a reservoir, intermediate sight.

items.q: length of curve may be defined as
o: a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines
the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
the fixed surface to which all reduced levels in a survey are referred
items.s: length of curve: the distance measured along the arc of the curve. The other options describe trapezoidal rule, temperature correction, datum.

items.q: Which term is described by “the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve”?
o: degree of curve
length of curve
simple circular curve
external distance
items.s: degree of curve is the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve.

items.q: Which term is described by “a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line”?
o: oblique offset
ill conditioned triangle
sag correction
optical square
items.s: optical square is a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines levelling?
o: the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
the operation of finding the difference in height between points
a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail
the amount by which the measured angles of a closed figure differ from the figure they should sum to
items.s: levelling: the operation of finding the difference in height between points. The other options describe capacity of a reservoir, angular misclosure, offset.

items.q: Which term is described by “positions of all stations measured from one common origin”?
o: angular misclosure
independent coordinates
transit rule
precision of a traverse
items.s: independent coordinates is positions of all stations measured from one common origin.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines sag correction?
o: the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line
the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
items.s: sag correction: the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports. The other options describe refraction correction, optical square, reduced level.

items.q: tension correction may be defined as
o: the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the allowance made because a tape stretches when the pull applied differs from the standard pull
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
items.s: tension correction: the allowance made because a tape stretches when the pull applied differs from the standard pull. The other options describe back bearing, true north, deflection angle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines gross error?
o: an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
items.s: gross error: a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument. The other options describe deflection angle of a curve, true north, total station.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines back bearing?
o: the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance
a surface every point of which is at the same height above mean sea level
items.s: back bearing: the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction. The other options describe level surface, levelling head, linear error of closure.

items.q: Which term is described by “the constant height difference between one contour and the next”?
o: planimeter
trapezoidal rule
contour interval
horizontal equivalent
items.s: contour interval is the constant height difference between one contour and the next.

items.q: The statement “the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve” describes which of the following?
o: degree of curve
point of curve
simple circular curve
external distance
items.s: external distance is the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve.

items.q: Which term is described by “the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging”?
o: refraction correction
reciprocal levelling
level surface
curvature correction
items.s: reciprocal levelling is the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging.

items.q: The statement “the smallest tilt of the telescope that visibly moves the bubble” describes which of the following?
o: line of collimation
sensitivity of a level
intermediate sight
level surface
items.s: sensitivity of a level is the smallest tilt of the telescope that visibly moves the bubble.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines whole circle bearing?
o: the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve
a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
items.s: whole circle bearing: a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees. The other options describe degree of curve, Simpson rule, random error.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tie line?
o: the eastward or westward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
a single line of a traverse, whose direction and length are measured
a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument
items.s: tie line: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework. The other options describe departure of a line, gross error, traverse leg.

items.q: Which term is described by “a surface every point of which is at the same height above mean sea level”?
o: datum
level surface
height of collimation
change point
items.s: level surface is a surface every point of which is at the same height above mean sea level.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines balancing a traverse.
o: a bookkeeping method in which consecutive staff readings are compared to show whether the ground rose or fell
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly
the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
items.s: balancing a traverse: the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly. The other options describe rise and fall, refraction correction, height of collimation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes standardisation of a tape?
o: the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
a short wooden stake driven into the ground to mark a station permanently
the process of comparing a tape against a known standard length and recording its error
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
items.s: standardisation of a tape: the process of comparing a tape against a known standard length and recording its error. The other options describe peg, mid ordinate, temperature correction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines consecutive coordinates?
o: the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
items.s: consecutive coordinates: positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before. The other options describe magnetic north, external distance, gross error.

items.q: closing error may be defined as
o: the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
the amount by which the measured angles of a closed figure differ from the figure they should sum to
the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
the short distance by which a closed traverse fails to return exactly to its starting station
items.s: closing error: the short distance by which a closed traverse fails to return exactly to its starting station. The other options describe height of instrument, angular misclosure, capacity of a reservoir.

items.q: Which of the following best describes contour?
o: the reduction applied when a distance is measured along sloping ground instead of horizontally
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
items.s: contour: a line joining points of equal height on the ground. The other options describe slope correction, differential correction, deflection angle.

items.q: Which term is described by “the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws”?
o: tribrach
electronic distance measurement
prism constant
levelling head
items.s: levelling head is the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines included angle?
o: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
the angle at a station between the two lines meeting there
items.s: included angle: the angle at a station between the two lines meeting there. The other options describe point of intersection, theodolite, quadrantal bearing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes linear misclosure?
o: the point where the straight ends and the curve begins
the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
a run of connected lines that returns to its starting point or closes on a known station
the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure
items.s: linear misclosure: the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure. The other options describe point of curve, curvature correction, closed traverse.

items.q: Which of the following best describes latitude of a line?
o: a painted pole set upright to mark a station or to keep a line straight
the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
items.s: latitude of a line: the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing. The other options describe ranging rod, whole circle bearing, levelling head.

items.q: The statement “the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve” describes which of the following?
o: degree of curve
point of intersection
tangent length
simple circular curve
items.s: degree of curve is the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve.

items.q: The statement “the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging” describes which of the following?
o: levelling
intermediate sight
height of collimation
reciprocal levelling
items.s: reciprocal levelling is the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging.

items.q: Which term is described by “the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing”?
o: planimeter
capacity of a reservoir
contour
Simpson rule
items.s: capacity of a reservoir is the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines transit rule.
o: the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line
a run of connected lines that returns to its starting point or closes on a known station
the angle at a station between the two lines meeting there
items.s: transit rule: the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line. The other options describe closed traverse, linear misclosure, included angle.

items.q: prism constant may be defined as
o: a bearing stated with reference to true north, measured clockwise
the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance
items.s: prism constant: the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing. The other options describe linear error of closure, mid ordinate, azimuth.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines grid north?
o: the distance measured along the arc of the curve
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle
items.s: grid north: the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted. The other options describe length of curve, deflection angle, exterior angle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines systematic error?
o: the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly
items.s: systematic error: an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out. The other options describe balancing a traverse, contour, tribrach.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines well conditioned triangle.
o: a triangle whose angles all lie between thirty and one hundred and twenty degrees, giving the strongest fix
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
items.s: well conditioned triangle: a triangle whose angles all lie between thirty and one hundred and twenty degrees, giving the strongest fix. The other options describe mid ordinate, reduced level, Simpson rule.

items.q: Which term is described by “the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level”?
o: sensitivity of a level
intermediate sight
datum
height of instrument
items.s: height of instrument is the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines bench mark.
o: a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling
positions of all stations measured from one common origin
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
items.s: bench mark: a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling. The other options describe temporary bench mark, consecutive coordinates, independent coordinates.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines perpendicular offset?
o: an offset that meets the survey line at exactly ninety degrees
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
items.s: perpendicular offset: an offset that meets the survey line at exactly ninety degrees. The other options describe length of curve, reduced level, deflection angle.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines versine.
o: the operation of finding the difference in height between points
the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
items.s: versine: the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle. The other options describe latitude of a line, interior angle, levelling.

items.q: refraction correction may be defined as
o: the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
positions of all stations measured from one common origin
a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines
items.s: refraction correction: the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect. The other options describe trapezoidal rule, independent coordinates, Simpson rule.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines versine?
o: the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle
the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
items.s: versine: the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle. The other options describe refraction correction, contour, latitude of a line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines degree of curve.
o: the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve
the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve
a bearing stated with reference to true north, measured clockwise
a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
items.s: degree of curve: the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve. The other options describe external distance, global positioning system, azimuth.

items.q: Which term is described by “the largest closing error that the specification for the work allows”?
o: permissible misclosure
accuracy
random error
precision
items.s: permissible misclosure is the largest closing error that the specification for the work allows.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 100 m reads 2.45 m and the foresight on the next point reads 2.8 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 100 + 2.45 = 102.5 m; reduced level = 102.5 - 2.8 = 99.65 m.

items.q: Convert the whole circle bearing of 55 degrees to a quadrantal bearing.
items.s: The bearing lies in the northeast quadrant, so the quadrantal bearing is 55 degrees NE.

items.q: The magnetic bearing of a line is 100 degrees and the magnetic declination at the place is 4 degrees east. Calculate the true bearing.
items.s: For easterly declination the true bearing is greater than the magnetic bearing: 100 + 4 = 104 degrees.

items.q: A traverse line is 100 m long and its bearing is 45 degrees. Calculate its departure in metres.
items.s: Departure = length x sine of the bearing = 100 x sin 45 = 70.71 m.

items.q: A closed traverse gives a total error in latitude of 300 m and a total error in departure of 200 m. Calculate the linear misclosure in metres.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (300 squared + 200 squared) = 360.6 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 80 m and a perpendicular height of 45 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 80 x 45 = 1800 square metres.

items.q: The cross sectional areas at the two ends of a cutting 25 m long are 30 and 30 square metres. Using the end area method, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = length x (first area + last area)/2 = 25 x (30 + 30)/2 = 750 cubic metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 250 m deflects through an angle of 70 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 250 x tan 35 = 175.1 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 250 m turns through a deflection angle of 40 degrees. Calculate the length of the curve in metres.
items.s: Length = pi x R x deflection / 180 = 3.1416 x 250 x 40 / 180 = 174.5 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 5000. A line on the plan measures 10 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 10 cm x 5000 = 50000 cm = 50000 m.

items.q: A tape of length 30 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 400000 N. It is used with a pull 50 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 50 x 30 / 400000 = 0.0037 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.3 N per metre is suspended between supports 30 m apart with a pull of 80 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.3 squared x 30 cubed / (24 x 80 squared) = 0.0158 m.

items.q: A backsight of 2.6 m is taken on a point of reduced level 125 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 125 + 2.6 = 127.6 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.6, 1.4 m and the falls recorded are 0.5, 1.15 m. The first point has a reduced level of 50 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 2 - 1.65 = 0.35 m, so the last reduced level is 50 + 0.35 = 50.35 m.

items.q: In levelling, the combined correction for curvature and refraction at a distance of 1 km is found from 0.0673 D squared. Calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = 0.0673 x 1 squared = 0.0673 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 0.8 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 0.84 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (0.8 + 0.84)/2 = 0.82 m.

items.q: The fore bearing of a line is 330 degrees. Calculate its back bearing.
items.s: Subtract 180 degrees: 330 - 180 = 150 degrees.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 160 degrees and 300 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 140 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 140 degrees.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 500 m and N 700 m. A line of length 90 m is run on a bearing of 30 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 90 x sin 30 = 45 m, so the new easting = 500 + 45 = 545 m.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 600 m has a closing error of 0.4 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 600 / 0.4 = 1 in 1500.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 4 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 45 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (4 - 2) x 180 = 360 degrees, so the measured angles are 360.8 degrees and the misclosure is 45 minutes.

items.q: A traverse of total length 500 m has a total error in departure of 0.4 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 80 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.4 x (80/500) = 0.064 m.

items.q: The offsets taken at 15 m intervals from a base line are 6, 4, 7, 2, 4 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 15[(6 + 4)/2 + 13] = 270 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 10 m intervals are 4, 8, 5, 6, 4 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 246.7 square metres.

items.q: In a cutting 20 m long the end areas are 30 and 50 square metres and the mid section area is 48 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 20/6[(30 + 50) + 4 x 48] = 906.7 cubic metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 40 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 10 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (10/40) x 100 = 25 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 250 m deflects through 60 degrees. Calculate the length of the long chord in metres.
items.s: Long chord = 2R sin(deflection/2) = 2 x 250 x sin 30 = 250 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m deflects through 40 degrees. Calculate the external distance in metres.
items.s: External = R[sec(deflection/2) - 1] = 100[sec 20 - 1] = 6.42 m.

items.q: A circular curve has a radius of 300 m. Taking the degree of curve as the angle subtended at the centre by an arc of 30 m, calculate that angle in degrees.
items.s: Degree of curve = 1718.87 / R = 1718.87 / 300 = 5.73 degrees.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 300 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 30 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 30 squared / (2 x 300) = 1.5 m.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 10 cm represents 10000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 10 cm to 1000000 cm, that is 1 in 100000 = 0.001.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 50 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 32 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 50 x 0.0000112 x 12 = 0.0067 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 200 m reads 1.25 m and the foresight on the next point reads 2.8 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 200 + 1.25 = 201.2 m; reduced level = 201.2 - 2.8 = 198.4 m.

items.q: A traverse line is 100 m long and its bearing is 35 degrees. Calculate its departure in metres.
items.s: Departure = length x sine of the bearing = 100 x sin 35 = 57.36 m.

items.q: A closed traverse gives a total error in latitude of 200 m and a total error in departure of 200 m. Calculate the linear misclosure in metres.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (200 squared + 200 squared) = 282.8 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 100 m and a perpendicular height of 40 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 100 x 40 = 2000 square metres.

items.q: The cross sectional areas at the two ends of a cutting 30 m long are 40 and 50 square metres. Using the end area method, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = length x (first area + last area)/2 = 30 x (40 + 50)/2 = 1350 cubic metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m deflects through an angle of 30 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 100 x tan 15 = 26.79 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 500. A line on the plan measures 12 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 12 cm x 500 = 6000 cm = 6000 m.

items.q: A tape of length 30 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 400000 N. It is used with a pull 20 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 20 x 30 / 400000 = 0.0015 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.25 N per metre is suspended between supports 30 m apart with a pull of 120 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.25 squared x 30 cubed / (24 x 120 squared) = 0.0049 m.

items.q: A backsight of 2.6 m is taken on a point of reduced level 110 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 110 + 2.6 = 112.6 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.45, 1.4 m and the falls recorded are 0.25, 0.35 m. The first point has a reduced level of 75 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 1.85 - 0.6 = 1.25 m, so the last reduced level is 75 + 1.25 = 76.25 m.

items.q: In levelling, the combined correction for curvature and refraction at a distance of 2 km is found from 0.0673 D squared. Calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = 0.0673 x 2 squared = 0.2692 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 1.2 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 1.24 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (1.2 + 1.24)/2 = 1.22 m.

items.q: The fore bearing of a line is 200 degrees. Calculate its back bearing.
items.s: Subtract 180 degrees: 200 - 180 = 20 degrees.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 160 degrees and 210 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 50 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 50 degrees.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 250 m and N 320 m. A line of length 90 m is run on a bearing of 50 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 90 x sin 50 = 68.94 m, so the new easting = 250 + 68.94 = 318.9 m.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 1000 m has a closing error of 0.5 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 1000 / 0.5 = 1 in 2000.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 4 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 90 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (4 - 2) x 180 = 360 degrees, so the measured angles are 361.5 degrees and the misclosure is 90 minutes.

items.q: A traverse of total length 800 m has a total error in departure of 0.4 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 100 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.4 x (100/800) = 0.05 m.

items.q: The offsets taken at 20 m intervals from a base line are 3, 6, 7, 4, 4 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 20[(3 + 4)/2 + 17] = 410 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 20 m intervals are 3, 6, 6, 8, 3 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 493.3 square metres.

items.q: In a cutting 30 m long the end areas are 40 and 40 square metres and the mid section area is 38 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 30/6[(40 + 40) + 4 x 38] = 1160 cubic metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 30 degrees. Calculate the length of the long chord in metres.
items.s: Long chord = 2R sin(deflection/2) = 2 x 150 x sin 15 = 77.65 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 300 m deflects through 90 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 300[1 - cos 45] = 87.87 m.

items.q: A circular curve has a radius of 200 m. Taking the degree of curve as the angle subtended at the centre by an arc of 30 m, calculate that angle in degrees.
items.s: Degree of curve = 1718.87 / R = 1718.87 / 200 = 8.59 degrees.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 400 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 10 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 10 squared / (2 x 400) = 0.125 m.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 10 cm represents 20000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 10 cm to 2000000 cm, that is 1 in 200000 = 0.0005.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 120 m reads 1.5 m and the foresight on the next point reads 3.15 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 120 + 1.5 = 121.5 m; reduced level = 121.5 - 3.15 = 118.3 m.

items.q: All of the following belong to Areas and volumes EXCEPT
o: planimeter
trapezoidal rule
linear misclosure
Simpson rule
items.s: Every other option belongs to Areas and volumes. “linear misclosure” belongs to Traversing and coordinates, not Areas and volumes.

items.q: The statement “the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted” describes which of the following?
o: bench mark
foresight
datum
sensitivity of a level
items.s: foresight is the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted.

items.q: In this course, closing error refers to
o: the ratio of the total length traversed to the closing error, stated as one in so many
the amount by which the measured angles of a closed figure differ from the figure they should sum to
the short distance by which a closed traverse fails to return exactly to its starting station
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line
items.s: closing error: the short distance by which a closed traverse fails to return exactly to its starting station. The other options describe transit rule, angular misclosure, precision of a traverse.

items.q: Choose the option that explains what mid ordinate means.
o: the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve
items.s: mid ordinate: the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve. The other options describe degree of curve, point of intersection, deflection angle of a curve.

items.q: The statement “a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly” describes which of the following?
o: standardisation of a tape
ranging rod
well conditioned triangle
chain surveying
items.s: chain surveying is a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly.

items.q: horizontal equivalent is best described as
o: the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
the constant height difference between one contour and the next
a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines
items.s: horizontal equivalent: the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map. The other options describe capacity of a reservoir, trapezoidal rule, contour interval.

items.q: The best definition of trapezoidal rule among these is
o: the constant height difference between one contour and the next
a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines
a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
items.s: trapezoidal rule: a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines. The other options describe end area method, contour interval, Simpson rule.
