items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 1.2, 1.4 m and the falls recorded are 0.5, 1.15 m. The first point has a reduced level of 120 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 2.6 - 1.65 = 0.95 m, so the last reduced level is 120 + 0.95 = 121 m.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 40 degrees and 210 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 170 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 170 degrees.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 500 m and N 700 m. A line of length 75 m is run on a bearing of 30 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 75 x sin 30 = 37.5 m, so the new easting = 500 + 37.5 = 537.5 m.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 600 m has a closing error of 0.25 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 600 / 0.25 = 1 in 2400.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 5 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 30 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (5 - 2) x 180 = 540 degrees, so the measured angles are 540.5 degrees and the misclosure is 30 minutes.

items.q: The offsets taken at 10 m intervals from a base line are 4, 4, 5, 3, 2 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 10[(4 + 2)/2 + 12] = 150 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 20 m intervals are 5, 6, 8, 6, 2 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 473.3 square metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through 60 degrees. Calculate the length of the long chord in metres.
items.s: Long chord = 2R sin(deflection/2) = 2 x 200 x sin 30 = 200 m.

items.q: A circular curve has a radius of 400 m. Taking the degree of curve as the angle subtended at the centre by an arc of 30 m, calculate that angle in degrees.
items.s: Degree of curve = 1718.87 / R = 1718.87 / 400 = 4.3 degrees.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 1000. A line on the plan measures 8 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 8 cm x 1000 = 8000 cm = 8000 m.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 25 cm represents 25000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 25 cm to 2500000 cm, that is 1 in 100000 = 0.001.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 30 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 28 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 30 x 0.0000112 x 8 = 0.0027 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.3 N per metre is suspended between supports 50 m apart with a pull of 80 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.3 squared x 50 cubed / (24 x 80 squared) = 0.0732 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 150 m reads 2.45 m and the foresight on the next point reads 0.75 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 150 + 2.45 = 152.4 m; reduced level = 152.4 - 0.75 = 151.7 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 1.2 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 1.22 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (1.2 + 1.22)/2 = 1.21 m.

items.q: The magnetic bearing of a line is 115 degrees and the magnetic declination at the place is 4 degrees east. Calculate the true bearing.
items.s: For easterly declination the true bearing is greater than the magnetic bearing: 115 + 4 = 119 degrees.

items.q: A traverse line is 100 m long and its bearing is 60 degrees. Calculate its latitude in metres.
items.s: Latitude = length x cosine of the bearing = 100 x cos 60 = 50 m.

items.q: A traverse of total length 800 m has a total error in departure of 0.5 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 50 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.5 x (50/800) = 0.0312 m.

items.q: The cross sectional areas at the two ends of a cutting 20 m long are 20 and 50 square metres. Using the end area method, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = length x (first area + last area)/2 = 20 x (20 + 50)/2 = 700 cubic metres.

items.q: In a cutting 20 m long the end areas are 30 and 40 square metres and the mid section area is 28 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 20/6[(30 + 40) + 4 x 28] = 606.7 cubic metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through an angle of 60 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 200 x tan 30 = 115.5 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m turns through a deflection angle of 50 degrees. Calculate the length of the curve in metres.
items.s: Length = pi x R x deflection / 180 = 3.1416 x 100 x 50 / 180 = 87.27 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 40 degrees. Calculate the external distance in metres.
items.s: External = R[sec(deflection/2) - 1] = 150[sec 20 - 1] = 9.63 m.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 400 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 30 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 30 squared / (2 x 400) = 1.12 m.

items.q: A tape of length 30 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 200000 N. It is used with a pull 60 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 60 x 30 / 200000 = 0.009 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.45, 0.75 m and the falls recorded are 0.25, 0.35 m. The first point has a reduced level of 120 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 1.2 - 0.6 = 0.6 m, so the last reduced level is 120 + 0.6 = 120.6 m.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 75 degrees and 240 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 165 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 165 degrees.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 250 m and N 320 m. A line of length 75 m is run on a bearing of 65 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 75 x sin 65 = 67.97 m, so the new easting = 250 + 67.97 = 318 m.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 6 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 60 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (6 - 2) x 180 = 720 degrees, so the measured angles are 721 degrees and the misclosure is 60 minutes.

items.q: The offsets taken at 15 m intervals from a base line are 3, 2, 5, 2, 7 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 15[(3 + 7)/2 + 9] = 210 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 20 m intervals are 6, 4, 2, 8, 8 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 440 square metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 20 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 2 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (2/20) x 100 = 10 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 90 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 150[1 - cos 45] = 43.93 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 1000. A line on the plan measures 4 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 4 cm x 1000 = 4000 cm = 4000 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.2 N per metre is suspended between supports 30 m apart with a pull of 100 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.2 squared x 30 cubed / (24 x 100 squared) = 0.0045 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 150 m reads 2.45 m and the foresight on the next point reads 3.15 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 150 + 2.45 = 152.4 m; reduced level = 152.4 - 3.15 = 149.3 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 0.6 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 0.62 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (0.6 + 0.62)/2 = 0.61 m.

items.q: Convert the whole circle bearing of 125 degrees to a quadrantal bearing.
items.s: The bearing lies in the northwest quadrant, so the quadrantal bearing is 55 degrees NW.

items.q: A traverse line is 80 m long and its bearing is 45 degrees. Calculate its departure in metres.
items.s: Departure = length x sine of the bearing = 80 x sin 45 = 56.57 m.

items.q: A closed traverse gives a total error in latitude of 100 m and a total error in departure of 200 m. Calculate the linear misclosure in metres.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (100 squared + 200 squared) = 223.6 m.

items.q: A traverse of total length 500 m has a total error in departure of 0.5 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 50 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.5 x (50/500) = 0.05 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 120 m and a perpendicular height of 20 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 120 x 20 = 1200 square metres.

items.q: The cross sectional areas at the two ends of a cutting 25 m long are 40 and 60 square metres. Using the end area method, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = length x (first area + last area)/2 = 25 x (40 + 60)/2 = 1250 cubic metres.

items.q: In a cutting 40 m long the end areas are 40 and 60 square metres and the mid section area is 48 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 40/6[(40 + 60) + 4 x 48] = 1947 cubic metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 250 m turns through a deflection angle of 60 degrees. Calculate the length of the curve in metres.
items.s: Length = pi x R x deflection / 180 = 3.1416 x 250 x 60 / 180 = 261.8 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 30 degrees. Calculate the external distance in metres.
items.s: External = R[sec(deflection/2) - 1] = 150[sec 15 - 1] = 5.29 m.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 200 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 40 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 40 squared / (2 x 200) = 4 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.45, 0.75 m and the falls recorded are 0.5, 0.35 m. The first point has a reduced level of 50 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 1.2 - 0.85 = 0.35 m, so the last reduced level is 50 + 0.35 = 50.35 m.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 110 degrees and 210 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 100 degrees, which is less than 180, so the included angle is 100 degrees.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 800 m has a closing error of 0.5 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 800 / 0.5 = 1 in 1600.

items.q: The offsets taken at 10 m intervals from a base line are 5, 5, 2, 6, 5 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 10[(5 + 5)/2 + 13] = 180 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 15 m intervals are 5, 2, 5, 5, 2 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 225 square metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 50 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 2 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (2/50) x 100 = 4 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through 40 degrees. Calculate the length of the long chord in metres.
items.s: Long chord = 2R sin(deflection/2) = 2 x 200 x sin 20 = 136.8 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 30 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 150[1 - cos 15] = 5.11 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 2000. A line on the plan measures 4 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 4 cm x 2000 = 8000 cm = 8000 m.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 30 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 30 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 30 x 0.0000112 x 10 = 0.0034 m.

items.q: A backsight of 2.6 m is taken on a point of reduced level 95 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 95 + 2.6 = 97.6 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 150 m reads 2 m and the foresight on the next point reads 0.75 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 150 + 2 = 152 m; reduced level = 152 - 0.75 = 151.2 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 0.8 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 0.86 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (0.8 + 0.86)/2 = 0.83 m.

items.q: Which of the following best describes angular misclosure?
o: the amount by which the measured angles of a closed figure differ from the figure they should sum to
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the length of each line
the ratio of the total length traversed to the closing error, stated as one in so many
a run of connected lines that does not return to its starting point
items.s: angular misclosure: the amount by which the measured angles of a closed figure differ from the figure they should sum to. The other options describe Bowditch rule, precision of a traverse, open traverse.

items.q: Which term is described by “a staff reading taken on a point that is neither a change point nor the closing sight”?
o: levelling
intermediate sight
level surface
curvature correction
items.s: intermediate sight is a staff reading taken on a point that is neither a change point nor the closing sight.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “software that stores, combines and displays mapped information”
o: tribrach
differential correction
geographic information system
tripod
items.s: geographic information system is software that stores, combines and displays mapped information.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines degree of curve?
o: the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
a curve of constant radius joining two straight lines
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
items.s: degree of curve: the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve. The other options describe simple circular curve, length of curve, deflection angle of a curve.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines precision?
o: the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance
a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument
how close a measurement comes to the true value
how closely repeated measurements agree with one another
items.s: precision: how closely repeated measurements agree with one another. The other options describe accuracy, gross error, linear error of closure.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines curvature correction.
o: the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
the smallest tilt of the telescope that visibly moves the bubble
the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
a staff reading taken on a point that is neither a change point nor the closing sight
items.s: curvature correction: the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance. The other options describe refraction correction, sensitivity of a level, intermediate sight.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines quadrantal bearing?
o: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
items.s: quadrantal bearing: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees. The other options describe fore bearing, grid north, back bearing.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed”
o: balancing a traverse
traverse
latitude of a line
linear misclosure
items.s: traverse is a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed.

items.q: levelling head is best described as
o: an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
items.s: levelling head: the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws. The other options describe theodolite, differential correction, global positioning system.

items.q: Which of the following best describes differential correction?
o: a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
items.s: differential correction: the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point. The other options describe global positioning system, levelling head, geographic information system.

items.q: Which of the following best describes magnetic north?
o: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
items.s: magnetic north: the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place. The other options describe interior angle, quadrantal bearing, grid north.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument”
o: permissible misclosure
systematic error
precision
gross error
items.s: gross error is a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument.

items.q: Which of the following best describes sag correction?
