the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports
a line measured only to prove that the plotted work is free of error
a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line
items.s: sag correction: the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports. The other options describe check line, optical square, peg.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines differential correction.
o: the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
items.s: differential correction: the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point. The other options describe tripod, global positioning system, theodolite.

items.q: intermediate sight is best described as
o: the first staff reading taken after the instrument is set up, on a point of known height
the operation of finding the difference in height between points
a staff reading taken on a point that is neither a change point nor the closing sight
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
items.s: intermediate sight: a staff reading taken on a point that is neither a change point nor the closing sight. The other options describe levelling, backsight, foresight.

items.q: transit rule is best described as
o: a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed
the ratio of the total length traversed to the closing error, stated as one in so many
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line
items.s: transit rule: the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line. The other options describe consecutive coordinates, traverse, precision of a traverse.

items.q: global positioning system may be defined as
o: the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing
a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
items.s: global positioning system: a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface. The other options describe levelling head, prism constant, electronic distance measurement.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail”
o: slope correction
tension correction
ill conditioned triangle
offset
items.s: offset is a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines local attraction.
o: the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current
items.s: local attraction: a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current. The other options describe fore bearing, magnetic north, grid north.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction”
o: fore bearing
whole circle bearing
quadrantal bearing
back bearing
items.s: back bearing is the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current”
o: grid north
local attraction
deflection angle
back bearing
items.s: local attraction is a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines peg.
o: a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly
a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak
the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
a short wooden stake driven into the ground to mark a station permanently
items.s: peg: a short wooden stake driven into the ground to mark a station permanently. The other options describe chain surveying, ill conditioned triangle, temperature correction.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point”
o: global positioning system
tribrach
geographic information system
differential correction
items.s: differential correction is the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point.

items.q: precision may be defined as
o: how close a measurement comes to the true value
the largest closing error that the specification for the work allows
an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
how closely repeated measurements agree with one another
items.s: precision: how closely repeated measurements agree with one another. The other options describe random error, accuracy, permissible misclosure.

items.q: local attraction may be defined as
o: a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle
the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
items.s: local attraction: a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current. The other options describe exterior angle, grid north, back bearing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes tripod?
o: the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
items.s: tripod: the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station. The other options describe tribrach, levelling head, electronic distance measurement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines trapezoidal rule.
o: a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines
an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
items.s: trapezoidal rule: a method of computing area that joins the ends of equally spaced offsets by straight lines. The other options describe contour, planimeter, horizontal equivalent.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely”
o: levelling head
total station
theodolite
global positioning system
items.s: theodolite is an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines linear error of closure.
o: a mistake caused by carelessness rather than by the limitation of the instrument
an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance
an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out
items.s: linear error of closure: the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance. The other options describe systematic error, gross error, random error.

items.q: Which term is described by “the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve”?
o: length of curve
tangent length
mid ordinate
point of tangency
items.s: mid ordinate is the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve.

items.q: tie line is best described as
o: a short wooden stake driven into the ground to mark a station permanently
the allowance made because a tape stretches when the pull applied differs from the standard pull
a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak
a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
items.s: tie line: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework. The other options describe ill conditioned triangle, tension correction, peg.

items.q: point of intersection may be defined as
o: the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
a curve of constant radius joining two straight lines
the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
items.s: point of intersection: the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted. The other options describe length of curve, point of tangency, simple circular curve.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “positions of all stations measured from one common origin”
o: closed traverse
consecutive coordinates
precision of a traverse
independent coordinates
items.s: independent coordinates is positions of all stations measured from one common origin.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline”
o: prismoidal formula
capacity of a reservoir
end area method
planimeter
items.s: planimeter is an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline.

items.q: tribrach may be defined as
o: software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
items.s: tribrach: the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred. The other options describe geographic information system, tripod, electronic distance measurement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines quadrantal bearing.
o: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
items.s: quadrantal bearing: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees. The other options describe whole circle bearing, grid north, interior angle.

items.q: tripod may be defined as
o: software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
items.s: tripod: the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station. The other options describe prism constant, electronic distance measurement, geographic information system.

items.q: height of collimation may be defined as
o: the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
items.s: height of collimation: the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum. The other options describe reduced level, line of collimation, foresight.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines ranging rod?
o: a triangle whose angles all lie between thirty and one hundred and twenty degrees, giving the strongest fix
a painted pole set upright to mark a station or to keep a line straight
an offset that meets the survey line at exactly ninety degrees
an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees
items.s: ranging rod: a painted pole set upright to mark a station or to keep a line straight. The other options describe oblique offset, well conditioned triangle, perpendicular offset.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines optical square.
o: a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail
the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
an offset that meets the survey line at exactly ninety degrees
a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line
items.s: optical square: a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line. The other options describe temperature correction, offset, perpendicular offset.

items.q: Which of the following best describes foresight?
o: the operation of finding the difference in height between points
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
items.s: foresight: the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted. The other options describe refraction correction, height of collimation, levelling.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised”
o: oblique offset
temperature correction
slope correction
tension correction
items.s: temperature correction is the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines contour?
o: a line joining points of equal height on the ground
a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
the constant height difference between one contour and the next
an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
items.s: contour: a line joining points of equal height on the ground. The other options describe planimeter, contour interval, end area method.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Bowditch rule.
o: the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
a run of connected lines that returns to its starting point or closes on a known station
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the length of each line
the eastward or westward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
items.s: Bowditch rule: the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the length of each line. The other options describe closed traverse, departure of a line, latitude of a line.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines fore bearing?
o: a bearing stated with reference to true north, measured clockwise
the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
items.s: fore bearing: the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress. The other options describe azimuth, back bearing, true north.

items.q: exterior angle may be defined as
o: the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle
a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
items.s: exterior angle: the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle. The other options describe deflection angle, whole circle bearing, magnetic north.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines tie line.
o: a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail
an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees
a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
the allowance made because a tape changes length as its temperature differs from the temperature at which it was standardised
items.s: tie line: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework. The other options describe offset, temperature correction, oblique offset.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines interior angle.
o: the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place
items.s: interior angle: the angle inside the closed figure at a station. The other options describe back bearing, magnetic declination, deflection angle.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines tribrach?
o: the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
items.s: tribrach: the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred. The other options describe tripod, prism constant, differential correction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes bench mark?
o: the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling
the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
items.s: bench mark: a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling. The other options describe refraction correction, line of collimation, curvature correction.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines refraction correction.
o: the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
items.s: refraction correction: the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect. The other options describe line of collimation, curvature correction, foresight.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines capacity of a reservoir.
o: an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
a volume rule that also takes account of the mid section, giving a closer result than averaging the two ends
the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
items.s: capacity of a reservoir: the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing. The other options describe planimeter, prismoidal formula, contour.

items.q: chain surveying may be defined as
o: an offset that meets the survey line at exactly ninety degrees
a triangle whose angles all lie between thirty and one hundred and twenty degrees, giving the strongest fix
the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports
a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly
items.s: chain surveying: a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly. The other options describe well conditioned triangle, perpendicular offset, sag correction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines levelling head?
o: software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
items.s: levelling head: the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws. The other options describe electronic distance measurement, differential correction, geographic information system.

items.q: Which of the following best describes long chord?
o: the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the straight line joining the start and end of the curve
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
the point where the straight ends and the curve begins
items.s: long chord: the straight line joining the start and end of the curve. The other options describe point of curve, mid ordinate, deflection angle of a curve.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight”
o: mid ordinate
deflection angle of a curve
long chord
versine
items.s: deflection angle of a curve is the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines true north?
o: the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place
a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
items.s: true north: the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation. The other options describe deflection angle, magnetic declination, quadrantal bearing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes fore bearing?
o: the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
items.s: fore bearing: the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress. The other options describe deflection angle, grid north, true north.

items.q: offset may be defined as
o: a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line
the allowance made because an unsupported tape dips below the straight line between its supports
a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail
a line measured only to prove that the plotted work is free of error
items.s: offset: a short measurement taken at right angles from a survey line to a detail. The other options describe check line, sag correction, optical square.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees”
o: azimuth
fore bearing
true north
quadrantal bearing
items.s: quadrantal bearing is a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines height of collimation?
o: the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling
items.s: height of collimation: the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum. The other options describe foresight, temporary bench mark, bench mark.

items.q: Which of the following best describes prism constant?
o: the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
the part of an instrument that carries the tribrach and the foot screws
an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing
items.s: prism constant: the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing. The other options describe total station, tribrach, levelling head.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines height of instrument?
o: a staff position that is read both before and after the instrument is moved
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
items.s: height of instrument: the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level. The other options describe reduced level, temporary bench mark, change point.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines exterior angle.
o: a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle
the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place
items.s: exterior angle: the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle. The other options describe whole circle bearing, magnetic declination, back bearing.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines ill conditioned triangle.
o: the longest and most carefully measured line of a chain survey from which the rest of the work is built
a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak
a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line
items.s: ill conditioned triangle: a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak. The other options describe tie line, base line, optical square.

items.q: A traverse of total length 800 m has a total error in departure of 0.8 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 80 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.8 x (80/800) = 0.08 m.

items.q: In a cutting 30 m long the end areas are 40 and 50 square metres and the mid section area is 48 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 30/6[(40 + 50) + 4 x 48] = 1410 cubic metres.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m deflects through 90 degrees. Calculate the external distance in metres.
items.s: External = R[sec(deflection/2) - 1] = 150[sec 45 - 1] = 62.13 m.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 100 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 30 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 30 squared / (2 x 100) = 4.5 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 5000. A line on the plan measures 4 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 4 cm x 5000 = 20000 cm = 20000 m.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 2 cm represents 4000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 2 cm to 400000 cm, that is 1 in 200000 = 0.0005.

items.q: A tape of length 30 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 200000 N. It is used with a pull 20 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 20 x 30 / 200000 = 0.003 m.

items.q: A backsight of 1.1 m is taken on a point of reduced level 125 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 125 + 1.1 = 126.1 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 100 m reads 2.45 m and the foresight on the next point reads 1.05 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 100 + 2.45 = 102.5 m; reduced level = 102.5 - 1.05 = 101.4 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.45, 1.4 m and the falls recorded are 0.25, 0.35 m. The first point has a reduced level of 50 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 1.85 - 0.6 = 1.25 m, so the last reduced level is 50 + 1.25 = 51.25 m.

items.q: The fore bearing of a line is 62 degrees. Calculate its back bearing.
items.s: Add 180 degrees: 62 + 180 = 242 degrees.

items.q: The magnetic bearing of a line is 115 degrees and the magnetic declination at the place is 6 degrees east. Calculate the true bearing.
items.s: For easterly declination the true bearing is greater than the magnetic bearing: 115 + 6 = 121 degrees.

items.q: A traverse line is 50 m long and its bearing is 35 degrees. Calculate its departure in metres.
items.s: Departure = length x sine of the bearing = 50 x sin 35 = 28.68 m.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 250 m and N 320 m. A line of length 75 m is run on a bearing of 30 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 75 x sin 30 = 37.5 m, so the new easting = 250 + 37.5 = 287.5 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 80 m and a perpendicular height of 40 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 80 x 40 = 1600 square metres.

items.q: The offsets taken at 20 m intervals from a base line are 6, 6, 2, 6, 2 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 20[(6 + 2)/2 + 14] = 360 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 15 m intervals are 3, 3, 3, 3, 6 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 195 square metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 40 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 2 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (2/40) x 100 = 5 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 200 m deflects through an angle of 70 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 200 x tan 35 = 140 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 150 m turns through a deflection angle of 50 degrees. Calculate the length of the curve in metres.
items.s: Length = pi x R x deflection / 180 = 3.1416 x 150 x 50 / 180 = 130.9 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m deflects through 40 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 100[1 - cos 20] = 6.03 m.

items.q: A tape of weight 0.25 N per metre is suspended between supports 50 m apart with a pull of 80 N. Calculate the sag correction in metres.
items.s: Sag correction = w squared x L cubed / (24 x P squared) = 0.25 squared x 50 cubed / (24 x 80 squared) = 0.0509 m.

items.q: A traverse of total length 800 m has a total error in departure of 0.4 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 50 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.4 x (50/800) = 0.025 m.

items.q: In a cutting 30 m long the end areas are 40 and 50 square metres and the mid section area is 28 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 30/6[(40 + 50) + 4 x 28] = 1010 cubic metres.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 400 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 40 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 40 squared / (2 x 400) = 2 m.

items.q: A plan is drawn to a scale of 1 : 2000. A line on the plan measures 5 cm. What is the corresponding horizontal distance on the ground in metres?
items.s: Ground distance = plan length x scale denominator = 5 cm x 2000 = 10000 cm = 10000 m.

items.q: On a plan a distance of 25 cm represents 125000 m on the ground. What is the representative fraction?
items.s: The ratio is 25 cm to 12500000 cm, that is 1 in 500000 = 0.0002.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 50 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 35 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 50 x 0.0000112 x 15 = 0.0084 m.

items.q: A tape of length 50 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 500000 N. It is used with a pull 40 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 40 x 50 / 500000 = 0.004 m.

items.q: A backsight of 1.1 m is taken on a point of reduced level 110 m. Calculate the height of the instrument.
items.s: Height of instrument = reduced level + backsight = 110 + 1.1 = 111.1 m.

items.q: A level is set up between two points. The backsight on a bench mark of reduced level 200 m reads 1.5 m and the foresight on the next point reads 1.05 m. Calculate the reduced level of the next point.
items.s: Height of instrument = 200 + 1.5 = 201.5 m; reduced level = 201.5 - 1.05 = 200.4 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.45, 0.3 m and the falls recorded are 0.9, 1.15 m. The first point has a reduced level of 50 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 0.75 - 2.05 = -1.3 m, so the last reduced level is 50 + -1.3 = 48.7 m.

items.q: Convert the whole circle bearing of 290 degrees to a quadrantal bearing.
items.s: The bearing lies in the southeast quadrant, so the quadrantal bearing is 70 degrees SE.

items.q: The magnetic bearing of a line is 100 degrees and the magnetic declination at the place is 5 degrees east. Calculate the true bearing.
items.s: For easterly declination the true bearing is greater than the magnetic bearing: 100 + 5 = 105 degrees.

items.q: A closed traverse gives a total error in latitude of 200 m and a total error in departure of 300 m. Calculate the linear misclosure in metres.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (200 squared + 300 squared) = 360.6 m.

items.q: A closed traverse of total length 600 m has a closing error of 0.2 m. State its precision as one in n.
items.s: Precision = total length / closing error = 600 / 0.2 = 1 in 3000.

items.q: The interior angles of a closed traverse of 6 sides are measured and their sum exceeds the theoretical sum by 30 minutes. Calculate the angular misclosure in minutes.
items.s: The theoretical sum is (6 - 2) x 180 = 720 degrees, so the measured angles are 720.5 degrees and the misclosure is 30 minutes.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 100 m and a perpendicular height of 45 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 100 x 45 = 2250 square metres.

items.q: The offsets taken at 10 m intervals from a base line are 2, 7, 2, 6, 3 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 10[(2 + 3)/2 + 15] = 175 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 10 m intervals are 3, 4, 6, 8, 4 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 223.3 square metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 40 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 5 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (5/40) x 100 = 12.5 percent.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 250 m deflects through an angle of 30 degrees. Calculate the tangent length in metres.
items.s: Tangent = R tan(deflection/2) = 250 x tan 15 = 66.99 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m turns through a deflection angle of 30 degrees. Calculate the length of the curve in metres.
items.s: Length = pi x R x deflection / 180 = 3.1416 x 100 x 30 / 180 = 52.36 m.

items.q: A simple circular curve of radius 100 m deflects through 30 degrees. Calculate the mid ordinate in metres.
items.s: Mid ordinate = R[1 - cos(deflection/2)] = 100[1 - cos 15] = 3.41 m.

items.q: In reciprocal levelling across a wide river the difference of level between the staff stations measured from the near bank is 0.4 m and the difference measured from the far bank is 0.44 m. Calculate the true difference of level in metres.
items.s: The two sights differ only by the combined instrumental error, so the true difference is their mean: (0.4 + 0.44)/2 = 0.42 m.

items.q: A traverse of total length 500 m has a total error in departure of 0.5 m. Using the Bowditch rule, calculate the correction to be applied to the departure of a line 100 m long, in metres.
items.s: Correction = total error x (length of line / total length) = 0.5 x (100/500) = 0.1 m.

items.q: In a cutting 20 m long the end areas are 30 and 40 square metres and the mid section area is 38 square metres. Using the prismoidal formula, calculate the volume in cubic metres.
items.s: Volume = L/6[(first + last) + 4(mid section)] = 20/6[(30 + 40) + 4 x 38] = 740 cubic metres.

items.q: A circular curve of radius 300 m is to be set out by offsets from the tangent. Calculate the offset at a distance of 10 m along the tangent, in metres.
items.s: Offset = x squared / (2R) = 10 squared / (2 x 300) = 0.1667 m.

items.q: A steel tape of nominal length 50 m was standardised at 20 degrees Celsius. It is used at a temperature of 30 degrees Celsius. Taking the coefficient of expansion as 0.0000112 per degree Celsius, calculate the correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = L x coefficient x (measured temperature - standard temperature) = 50 x 0.0000112 x 10 = 0.0056 m.

items.q: A tape of length 30 m has a cross sectional area times modulus of elasticity of 400000 N. It is used with a pull 60 N greater than the standard pull. Calculate the tension correction in metres.
items.s: Correction = (applied pull - standard pull) x length / (area x modulus) = 60 x 30 / 400000 = 0.0045 m.

items.q: In a level book the rises recorded are 0.6, 1.4 m and the falls recorded are 0.25, 0.35 m. The first point has a reduced level of 60 m. Calculate the reduced level of the last point.
items.s: Net change = sum of rises - sum of falls = 2 - 0.6 = 1.4 m, so the last reduced level is 60 + 1.4 = 61.4 m.

items.q: Convert the whole circle bearing of 70 degrees to a quadrantal bearing.
items.s: The bearing lies in the northeast quadrant, so the quadrantal bearing is 70 degrees NE.

items.q: The bearings of two lines meeting at a station are 110 degrees and 300 degrees. Calculate the included angle between them.
items.s: The difference of the bearings is 190 degrees, so the included angle is 360 - 190 = 170 degrees.

items.q: A traverse line is 120 m long and its bearing is 35 degrees. Calculate its departure in metres.
items.s: Departure = length x sine of the bearing = 120 x sin 35 = 68.83 m.

items.q: A station has coordinates E 250 m and N 320 m. A line of length 60 m is run on a bearing of 30 degrees. Calculate the easting of the next station in metres.
items.s: Departure = 60 x sin 30 = 30 m, so the new easting = 250 + 30 = 280 m.

items.q: A closed traverse gives a total error in latitude of 300 m and a total error in departure of 400 m. Calculate the linear misclosure in metres.
items.s: Misclosure = square root of (300 squared + 400 squared) = 500 m.

items.q: A triangle of ground has a base of 100 m and a perpendicular height of 30 m. Calculate its area in square metres.
items.s: Area = half x base x height = 0.5 x 100 x 30 = 1500 square metres.

items.q: The offsets taken at 15 m intervals from a base line are 3, 5, 3, 6, 3 m. Using the trapezoidal rule, calculate the area enclosed in square metres.
items.s: Area = h[(first + last)/2 + sum of the others] = 15[(3 + 3)/2 + 14] = 255 square metres.

items.q: Five offsets taken at 20 m intervals are 2, 5, 2, 8, 2 m. Using Simpson rule, calculate the area in square metres.
items.s: Area = h/3[(first + last) + 4(sum of odd offsets) + 2(sum of even offsets)] = 400 square metres.

items.q: Two adjacent contours are 25 m apart on the ground and the contour interval is 2 m. Calculate the average slope between them as a percentage.
items.s: Slope = (contour interval / horizontal equivalent) x 100 = (2/25) x 100 = 8 percent.

items.q: In this course, change point refers to
o: the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
a staff position that is read both before and after the instrument is moved
a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling
the fixed surface to which all reduced levels in a survey are referred
items.s: change point: a staff position that is read both before and after the instrument is moved. The other options describe datum, height of collimation, bench mark.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation”
o: magnetic north
traverse leg
whole circle bearing
true north
items.s: true north is the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation.

items.q: In this course, contour refers to
o: the constant height difference between one contour and the next
the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
items.s: contour: a line joining points of equal height on the ground. The other options describe end area method, horizontal equivalent, contour interval.

items.q: In this course, balancing a traverse refers to
o: the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly
the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure
the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
positions of all stations measured from one common origin
items.s: balancing a traverse: the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly. The other options describe linear misclosure, latitude of a line, independent coordinates.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines horizontal equivalent?
o: the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
a volume rule that also takes account of the mid section, giving a closer result than averaging the two ends
items.s: horizontal equivalent: the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map. The other options describe capacity of a reservoir, prismoidal formula, end area method.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines differential correction?
o: the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
items.s: differential correction: the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point. The other options describe tribrach, theodolite, tripod.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains quadrantal bearing.
o: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
items.s: quadrantal bearing: a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees. The other options describe back bearing, fore bearing, magnetic north.

items.q: “the eastward or westward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing” is the definition of
o: balancing a traverse
Bowditch rule
departure of a line
consecutive coordinates
items.s: departure of a line is the eastward or westward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing.

items.q: In this course, transit rule refers to
o: a run of connected lines that does not return to its starting point
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line
the short distance by which a closed traverse fails to return exactly to its starting station
a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed
items.s: transit rule: the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the latitude and departure of each line. The other options describe open traverse, traverse, closing error.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains foresight.
o: the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging
the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
items.s: foresight: the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted. The other options describe reciprocal levelling, height of instrument, line of collimation.

items.q: “the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted” is the definition of
o: traverse leg
exterior angle
grid north
back bearing
items.s: grid north is the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted.

items.q: In this course, long chord refers to
o: the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
the straight line joining the start and end of the curve
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
items.s: long chord: the straight line joining the start and end of the curve. The other options describe point of intersection, deflection angle of a curve, mid ordinate.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains prism constant.
o: the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing
the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
items.s: prism constant: the fixed addition made to a measured distance to allow for the reflector housing. The other options describe tribrach, electronic distance measurement, total station.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains exterior angle.
o: the direction of a line measured in the direction of progress
the angle at a station between the two lines meeting there
the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
items.s: exterior angle: the angle outside the closed figure at a station, being three hundred and sixty degrees less the interior angle. The other options describe interior angle, fore bearing, included angle.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains reduced level.
o: a permanent mark of known height used as a starting point for levelling
the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
items.s: reduced level: the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum. The other options describe line of collimation, bench mark, temporary bench mark.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains end area method.
o: a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
items.s: end area method: a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length. The other options describe planimeter, horizontal equivalent, Simpson rule.

items.q: reduced level may be defined as
o: the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
items.s: reduced level: the height of a point stated with reference to the chosen datum. The other options describe foresight, height of instrument, height of collimation.

items.q: curvature correction may be defined as
o: the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
the fixed surface to which all reduced levels in a survey are referred
the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
the bending of the line of sight towards the earth, which partly cancels the curvature effect
items.s: curvature correction: the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance. The other options describe datum, height of instrument, refraction correction.

items.q: In this course, Simpson rule refers to
o: the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
a line joining points of equal height on the ground
a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
items.s: Simpson rule: a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets. The other options describe capacity of a reservoir, contour, planimeter.

items.q: The correct meaning of length of curve is
o: the distance measured along the arc of the curve
the straight line joining the start and end of the curve
the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve
the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle
items.s: length of curve: the distance measured along the arc of the curve. The other options describe external distance, versine, long chord.

items.q: “a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length” is the definition of
o: planimeter
contour
end area method
horizontal equivalent
items.s: end area method is a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length.

items.q: In this course, point of intersection refers to
o: the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle
the distance from the point of intersection to the start or end of the curve
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
items.s: point of intersection: the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted. The other options describe tangent length, deflection angle of a curve, versine.

items.q: “the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle” is the definition of
o: mid ordinate
versine
long chord
point of curve
items.s: versine is the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains tie line.
o: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly
a line measured only to prove that the plotted work is free of error
a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak
items.s: tie line: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework. The other options describe chain surveying, ill conditioned triangle, check line.

items.q: “the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins” is the definition of
o: point of tangency
external distance
tangent length
deflection angle of a curve
items.s: point of tangency is the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains differential correction.
o: the fitting that attaches an instrument to the tripod and allows it to be centred
software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
items.s: differential correction: the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point. The other options describe geographic information system, tribrach, total station.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains point of tangency.
o: the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins
the point where the straight ends and the curve begins
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve
items.s: point of tangency: the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins. The other options describe point of curve, external distance, length of curve.

items.q: “the angle inside the closed figure at a station” is the definition of
o: magnetic declination
interior angle
azimuth
true north
items.s: interior angle is the angle inside the closed figure at a station.

items.q: The correct meaning of balancing a traverse is
o: the eastward or westward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed
items.s: balancing a traverse: the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly. The other options describe consecutive coordinates, departure of a line, traverse.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains temporary bench mark.
o: the straight line through the centre of the objective and the cross hairs of a level
the fall of the earth surface away from a horizontal line of sight, which grows with the square of the distance
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
items.s: temporary bench mark: a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only. The other options describe line of collimation, height of collimation, curvature correction.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains traverse.
o: the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
the length of the closing error, found by combining the errors in latitude and departure
a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed
the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly
items.s: traverse: a framework of connected lines whose directions and lengths are measured so that the positions of the stations can be computed. The other options describe balancing a traverse, linear misclosure, latitude of a line.

items.q: Three of these relate to Errors and adjustments. Which one does not?
o: temporary bench mark
gross error
random error
systematic error
items.s: Every other option belongs to Errors and adjustments. “temporary bench mark” belongs to Levelling, not Errors and adjustments.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines global positioning system?
o: software that stores, combines and displays mapped information
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
items.s: global positioning system: a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface. The other options describe geographic information system, electronic distance measurement, differential correction.

items.q: “a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak” is the definition of
o: ill conditioned triangle
tie line
optical square
slope correction
items.s: ill conditioned triangle is a triangle with a very small angle, in which the plotted position is weak.

items.q: traverse leg may be defined as
o: a single line of a traverse, whose direction and length are measured
a direction stated as an angle from north or south towards east or west, and never above ninety degrees
the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the angle inside the closed figure at a station
items.s: traverse leg: a single line of a traverse, whose direction and length are measured. The other options describe interior angle, quadrantal bearing, deflection angle.

items.q: The correct meaning of true north is
o: the angle by which a line turns away from the continuation of the previous line
the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place
the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
items.s: true north: the direction of the earth axis at a place, found from astronomical observation. The other options describe magnetic north, magnetic declination, deflection angle.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the fixed surface to which all reduced levels in a survey are referred”
o: rise and fall
datum
change point
reduced level
items.s: datum is the fixed surface to which all reduced levels in a survey are referred.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains mid ordinate.
o: a curve of constant radius joining two straight lines
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve
the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve
items.s: mid ordinate: the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve. The other options describe simple circular curve, external distance, degree of curve.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the reduction applied when a distance is measured along sloping ground instead of horizontally”
o: chain surveying
sag correction
base line
slope correction
items.s: slope correction is the reduction applied when a distance is measured along sloping ground instead of horizontally.

items.q: oblique offset may be defined as
o: a triangle whose angles all lie between thirty and one hundred and twenty degrees, giving the strongest fix
a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
a method in which lengths are measured with a chain or tape and no angles are observed directly
an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees
items.s: oblique offset: an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees. The other options describe well conditioned triangle, chain surveying, tie line.

items.q: In this course, foresight refers to
o: the method of levelling across a wide river by taking sights from both banks and averaging
the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted
the smallest tilt of the telescope that visibly moves the bubble
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
items.s: foresight: the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted. The other options describe temporary bench mark, reciprocal levelling, sensitivity of a level.

items.q: In this course, simple circular curve refers to
o: a curve of constant radius joining two straight lines
the distance from the point of intersection to the start or end of the curve
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
items.s: simple circular curve: a curve of constant radius joining two straight lines. The other options describe tangent length, deflection angle of a curve, length of curve.

items.q: “the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve” is the definition of
o: mid ordinate
external distance
degree of curve
long chord
items.s: external distance is the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted”
o: grid north
traverse leg
azimuth
quadrantal bearing
items.s: grid north is the direction of the central meridian of the map grid on which the survey is plotted.

items.q: In this course, theodolite refers to
o: an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
a satellite service that gives position and height anywhere on the earth surface
an instrument that measures both angles and distances and stores them electronically
items.s: theodolite: an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely. The other options describe global positioning system, electronic distance measurement, total station.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines length of curve?
o: the distance from the point of intersection to the start or end of the curve
the point where the straight ends and the curve begins
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
items.s: length of curve: the distance measured along the arc of the curve. The other options describe point of intersection, point of curve, tangent length.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains latitude of a line.
o: the operation of distributing the closing error so that the figure closes exactly
the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing
the adjustment of a traverse by sharing the closing error in proportion to the length of each line
positions of traverse stations measured from the station immediately before
items.s: latitude of a line: the northward or southward distance covered by the line, found from its length and bearing. The other options describe balancing a traverse, Bowditch rule, consecutive coordinates.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the straight line joining the start and end of the curve”
o: long chord
deflection angle of a curve
simple circular curve
mid ordinate
items.s: long chord is the straight line joining the start and end of the curve.

items.q: In this course, end area method refers to
o: the ground distance between two adjacent contours on a map
a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
the constant height difference between one contour and the next
an instrument that gives the area of a plotted figure by tracing its outline
items.s: end area method: a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length. The other options describe horizontal equivalent, planimeter, contour interval.

items.q: The correct meaning of change point is
o: a staff position that is read both before and after the instrument is moved
a surface every point of which is at the same height above mean sea level
a bookkeeping method in which consecutive staff readings are compared to show whether the ground rose or fell
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
items.s: change point: a staff position that is read both before and after the instrument is moved. The other options describe height of collimation, rise and fall, level surface.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted”
o: intermediate sight
reduced level
backsight
foresight
items.s: foresight is the last staff reading taken before the instrument is moved, on the point whose height is wanted.

items.q: The correct meaning of magnetic north is
o: a bearing stated with reference to true north, measured clockwise
the direction of the same line measured in the reverse direction
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
a direction measured clockwise from north through the full range from zero to three hundred and sixty degrees
items.s: magnetic north: the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place. The other options describe whole circle bearing, azimuth, back bearing.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains level surface.
o: a surface every point of which is at the same height above mean sea level
the first staff reading taken after the instrument is set up, on a point of known height
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
a firm point of known height established for use during one piece of work only
items.s: level surface: a surface every point of which is at the same height above mean sea level. The other options describe height of collimation, backsight, temporary bench mark.

items.q: The correct meaning of deflection angle of a curve is
o: the point where the straight ends and the curve begins
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
the point where the two straights would meet if the curve were not inserted
the distance from the point of intersection to the middle of the curve
items.s: deflection angle of a curve: the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight. The other options describe point of intersection, external distance, point of curve.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains magnetic declination.
o: a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by nearby iron, steel or electric current
a single line of a traverse, whose direction and length are measured
the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place
the direction shown by a freely suspended magnetic needle at a place
items.s: magnetic declination: the angle between true north and magnetic north at a place. The other options describe magnetic north, traverse leg, local attraction.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains systematic error.
o: an error that acts sometimes one way and sometimes the other, so it tends to cancel in a mean
an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out
how close a measurement comes to the true value
the largest closing error that the specification for the work allows
items.s: systematic error: an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out. The other options describe permissible misclosure, accuracy, random error.

items.q: The correct meaning of tripod is
o: an instrument for measuring horizontal and vertical angles precisely
the determination of a distance from the travel time or phase difference of a transmitted signal
the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station
the improvement of a satellite position by comparing it with a receiver at a known point
items.s: tripod: the three legged stand that carries a surveying instrument and is set level over a station. The other options describe differential correction, theodolite, electronic distance measurement.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains versine.
o: the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins
the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle
the angle between the first straight produced and the second straight
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
items.s: versine: the small height between the chord and the arc, equal to the radius less the radius times the cosine of half the angle. The other options describe deflection angle of a curve, mid ordinate, point of tangency.

items.q: systematic error may be defined as
o: how closely repeated measurements agree with one another
an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out
how close a measurement comes to the true value
the misclosure of a closed figure already expressed as a distance
items.s: systematic error: an error that acts the same way in every reading, so it does not average out. The other options describe precision, accuracy, linear error of closure.

items.q: tie line may be defined as
o: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework
the longest and most carefully measured line of a chain survey from which the rest of the work is built
the reduction applied when a distance is measured along sloping ground instead of horizontally
a small hand instrument used to set out a right angle at a point on a line
items.s: tie line: a line run to check the position of a station that is not on the main framework. The other options describe base line, optical square, slope correction.

items.q: The correct meaning of mid ordinate is
o: the central angle subtended by a stated standard arc length of the curve
the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins
the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve
the distance from the point of intersection to the start or end of the curve
items.s: mid ordinate: the distance from the middle of the long chord to the middle of the curve. The other options describe point of tangency, tangent length, degree of curve.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains capacity of a reservoir.
o: a method of computing volume from the cross sectional areas at the two ends of a length
the constant height difference between one contour and the next
the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing
a method of computing area that fits a parabolic curve through groups of three equally spaced offsets
items.s: capacity of a reservoir: the volume of water a depression can hold, found from contour areas and their spacing. The other options describe Simpson rule, end area method, contour interval.

items.q: The correct meaning of levelling is
o: the operation of finding the difference in height between points
the fixed surface to which all reduced levels in a survey are referred
the alternative name for the height of the line of sight above the datum
the height of the line of sight above the datum after a backsight has been added to the reduced level
items.s: levelling: the operation of finding the difference in height between points. The other options describe height of collimation, datum, height of instrument.

items.q: “an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees” is the definition of
o: base line
oblique offset
tie line
sag correction
items.s: oblique offset is an offset that meets the survey line at an angle other than ninety degrees.

items.q: point of tangency may be defined as
o: a curve of constant radius joining two straight lines
the point where the straight ends and the curve begins
the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins
the distance measured along the arc of the curve
items.s: point of tangency: the point where the curve ends and the next straight begins. The other options describe point of curve, length of curve, simple circular curve.
